texts: bad: "in the present generation" is hung on the group of Keepers as a standing relation between two things, while the rule that carries the real claim says only that each of those Keepers is active — the restriction never reaches the predication, so the parse asserts the Keepers are active flat out, a wider claim than you made. Let the generation restrict the Keepers themselves instead of framing the clause: "Forty-three Keepers of the present generation are active." That keeps the count, the generation and the activeness, and the per-member conclusion is then limited to that generation's Keepers.

good. the three apprentices keep their count and group, the lanterns are a group belonging to Aelmere, and the per-apprentice tending rule ranges over the group, so an apprentice named later inherits a tending of those lanterns.
